name: Keeping knowledge as data changes over time
gist: Papers tackle continual learning and domain adaptation by building models that learn from new data without forgetting old knowledge, important for real-world systems that must evolve.
explain: In the real world, data arrives continuously. A factory's production process shifts, social media trends change, new species of plants appear in ecology datasets. When a model is trained once and deployed, it sees data it was never trained on, and its performance decays — a phenomenon called distribution shift or domain adaptation. Simply retraining the model from scratch on new data is expensive and often causes catastrophic forgetting: the model forgets everything it learned before and has to relearn it all. The goal is to learn from new data without erasing old knowledge.

This is genuinely hard because neural networks are prone to interference: fitting new patterns can mechanically overwrite the weights that encoded old patterns. Continual learning researchers explore several strategies: maintain a buffer of past data and mix it with new data when training, learn in a way that is less destructive to old knowledge (like constraining weight changes), develop architectures that isolate new tasks in dedicated pathways, or learn features that are more stable across domains. The tradeoff is always the same: if you are too conservative with old knowledge, you learn slowly from new data; if you are too aggressive, you forget. Finding that balance is the core research question.

Across 57 papers, researchers tackle continual learning, domain adaptation, and few-shot learning (learning from very few examples of a new domain). Some papers ask what the theoretical limits are: is it possible to never forget? Others build practical systems: test-time adaptation methods that adjust the model slightly as it encounters new data, or meta-learning approaches that train the model to learn quickly from new examples. The applications are critical: robots deployed in the real world need to adapt, medical AI systems need to handle new patient populations, and recommendation systems need to track evolving user preferences.

papers.title: CoMem: Compositional Concept-Graph Memory for Vision–Language Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art retention and transfer with consistent gains on cross-domain retrieval, concept learning, and continual VQA under matched memory and parameter budgets.

papers.title: Detect, Decide, Unlearn: A Transfer-Aware Framework for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: DEDUCE achieves average accuracy improvements of up to 5.5% over state-of-the-art baselines by mitigating task interference in continual learning.

papers.title: FedPAT: Federated Test-Time Adaptation via Prototype Affinity Topology
papers.contribution: FedPAT consistently outperforms federated and classical test-time adaptation methods across various distribution shifts by leveraging stable prototype relationships.

papers.title: Fly-CL: A Fly-Inspired Framework for Enhancing Efficient Decorrelation and Reduced Training Time in Pre-trained Model-based Continual Repres
papers.contribution: Substantially reduces training time while achieving performance comparable to or exceeding state-of-the-art methods with theoretical justification.

papers.title: HEDP: A Hybrid Energy-Distance Prompt-based Framework for Domain Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 2.57% accuracy improvement on unseen domains, effectively mitigating catastrophic forgetting with enhanced open-world adaptability.

papers.title: IDER: IDEMPOTENT EXPERIENCE REPLAY FOR RELIABLE CONTINUAL LEARNING
papers.contribution: Consistently improves prediction reliability, accuracy, and reduces forgetting across benchmarks while maintaining compatibility with mainstream replay methods.

papers.title: Long-tailed Test-Time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Superior performance across 15 datasets under various long-tailed settings in both accuracy and class balancing.

papers.title: MoCL: Metabolic Optimization for Curvature-Aware Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both classification performance and efficiency by capturing geometric manifolds while supporting shared low-loss behavior.

papers.title: Personalized Feature Translation for Expression Recognition: An Efficient Source-Free Domain Adaptation Method
papers.contribution: Improves facial expression recognition performance through latent-space feature translation without requiring source data or computationally intensive face image generation.

papers.title: RC-FCL: Combating Asynchronous Concept Drift in Federated Continual Learning via Retrospective Calibration
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive performance against state-of-the-art with effective distinction of asynchronous concept drift and adaptive learning strategies.

papers.title: Task-Driven Subspace Decomposition for Knowledge Sharing and Isolation in LoRA-based Continual Learning
papers.contribution: LoDA outperforms existing continual learning methods by decoupling knowledge sharing and isolation while maintaining robust performance.

papers.title: Adaptive Debiasing Tsallis Entropy for Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Proposes Adaptive Debiasing Tsallis Entropy (ADTE) that outperforms state-of-the-art on ImageNet and 10 cross-domain benchmarks without hyperparameter tuning.

papers.title: Avoid Catastrophic Forgetting with Rank-1 Fisher from Diffusion Models
papers.contribution: Consistently improves average FID and reduces forgetting; nearly eliminates on MNIST/FashionMNIST and roughly halves on ImageNet-1k.

papers.title: BTSP-CAM: A Brain-Inspired Geometric Memory for Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Rivals gradient-based methods in exemplar-free settings; consistently boosts SOTA baselines as a lightweight plugin with mechanistic validation of geometric theory.

papers.title: Bilateral Information-aware Test-time Adaptation for Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: The dual approach prevents undesired memorization and ensures optimal performance across datasets and model architectures.

papers.title: CE$^4$L: Continual Ego, Exo, and Ego-Exo Learning
papers.contribution: Reveals challenges absent in prior CL benchmarks; VISTA achieves state-of-the-art overall performance with parameter efficiency.

papers.title: Capacity-Agnostic Parameter Isolation for Continual Graph Learning
papers.contribution: The framework demonstrates superior effectiveness and computational efficiency over state-of-the-art continual learning methods.

papers.title: Consistency-Driven Calibration and Matching for Few-Shot Class Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: ConCM achieves state-of-the-art performance with harmonic accuracy gains up to 3.41% on mini-ImageNet, CIFAR100, and CUB200 benchmarks.

papers.title: Continual Learning of Domain-Invariant Representations
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms CL baselines on generalization to unseen domains across vision, medicine, manufacturing, and ecology benchmarks.

papers.title: Cross-View Lewis Weight Fusion Empowering Exemplar Replay for Federated Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently improves baselines by 1-6% with theoretical guarantees for soundness.

papers.title: Decoupling Primitive with Experts: Dynamic Feature Alignment for Compositional Zero-Shot Learning
papers.contribution: EVA significantly outperforms state-of-the-art CZSL methods on three benchmarks in both closed- and open-world settings.

papers.title: Demystifying Mergeability: Interpretable Properties to Predict Model Merging Success
papers.contribution: Reveals drivers of merge success vary across architectures with only moderate agreement (64.0% top-5 overlap), but gradient alignment consistently emerges as most fundamental signal enabling diagnostic foundation for mergeability.

papers.title: ECA: Efficient Continual Alignment for Open-Ended Image-to-Text Generation
papers.contribution: Significantly mitigates catastrophic forgetting; outperforms baselines on four new IL benchmarks reflecting real-world scenarios.

papers.title: ELViS: Efficient Visual Similarity from Local Descriptors that Generalizes Across Domains
papers.contribution: ELViS outperforms competing methods by a large margin in out-of-domain scenarios while requiring only a fraction of their computational cost.

papers.title: Factor-Wise Homogeneity of Slot-Attention for Continual Object-Centric Learning
papers.contribution: Factor-wise homogeneity serves as key mechanism preventing forgetting in continual object-centric learning, achievable with minimal intervention.

papers.title: Forgetting Whenever You Want: A Decentralized Continual Learning Framework with On-Demand Unlearning
papers.contribution: DCU achieves effective class continual learning and arbitrary-time class unlearning in distributed settings with minimal performance degradation.

papers.title: GR-LoRA: Gradient-Recycling Low-Rank Adaptation for Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Preserves stability and improves plasticity with theoretical confirmation, experimental validation across multiple CIL benchmarks verifies effectiveness and general applicability.

papers.title: HypCL: Adapting CLIP in Hyperbolic Space for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms existing CLIP-based continual learning methods on class-incremental benchmarks with better feature separability.

papers.title: JANUS-LORA: A Balanced Low-Rank Adaptation for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves superior stability-plasticity balance and state-of-the-art performance on continual learning benchmarks.

papers.title: LCA: Local Classifier Alignment for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: LCA often achieves leading performance on standard continual learning benchmarks, sometimes surpassing state-of-the-art methods with a large margin.

papers.title: Learn to Merge: Meta-Learning for Adaptive Multi-Task Model Merging
papers.contribution: Produces more balanced and generalizable unified models with strong performance across CV and NLP downstream tasks compared to parameter merging methods.

papers.title: Learning to Memorize with Attributive and Associative Memory for Online Test-Time Adaptation of Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Demonstrates consistent improvements over state-of-the-art methods across 15 benchmarks.

papers.title: MePo: Meta Post-Refinement for Rehearsal-Free General Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 15.10% improvement on CIFAR-100, 13.36% on ImageNet-R, and 12.56% on CUB-200 in rehearsal-free continual learning without needing task boundaries.

papers.title: Merge to Remember: Sharpness-Aware Isotropic Merging for Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Achieves 5-10% higher accuracy than existing methods while maintaining robust performance as task count increases, with code available.

papers.title: MergeTune: Continued Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language Models
papers.contribution: Improves harmonic mean of CoOp by 5.6% on base-novel generalization and achieves state-of-the-art results on robust fine-tuning evaluations.

papers.title: Mixing Expertise with Confidence: A Mixture of Experts Framework for Robust Multi-Modal Continual Learning
papers.contribution: The approach consistently outperforms existing methods across diverse continual learning settings without requiring reference datasets or replay memory, with new evaluation benchmarks simulating realistic scenarios.

papers.title: Multi-Synaptic Cooperation: A Bio-Inspired Framework for Robust and Scalable Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art continual learning methods with significantly improved robustness to task-order variation across spiking and non-spiking networks.

papers.title: On the Power of Statistics in Class-Incremental Learning with Pretrained Models
papers.contribution: Competitive performance on class-incremental learning can be achieved via class-level inference based solely on statistical estimators from frozen features.

papers.title: One-Prompt Strikes Back: Sparse Mixture of Experts for Prompt-based Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Outperforms task-specific prompt methods while achieving efficiency comparable to single-prompt approaches across multiple CL benchmarks.

papers.title: Online Continual Learning with Dynamic Label Hierarchies
papers.contribution: Enable rapid adaptation and hierarchical consistency as taxonomy evolves, outperforming existing methods on hierarchical accuracy and catastrophic forgetting.

papers.title: PACE: Pretrained Audio Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms state-of-the-art baselines across six diverse audio continual learning benchmarks.

papers.title: PLATE: Plasticity-Tunable Efficient Adapters for Geometry-Aware Continual Learning
papers.contribution: Provides explicit control over plasticity-retention trade-off without past-task data access and maintains worst-case retention guarantees.

papers.title: Parameter-Masked Decoupled Optimization for Cross-Domain Class-Incremental Learning
papers.contribution: Enables effective cross-domain adaptation while mitigating catastrophic forgetting and maintaining long-term learnability across benchmarks.

papers.title: Quantized Gradient Projection for Memory-Efficient Continual Learning
papers.contribution: QGPM achieves state-of-the-art performance under fixed memory budgets, demonstrating effectiveness in scalable, privacy-preserving continual learning.

papers.title: Rethinking Continual Learning with Progressive Neural Collapse
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms baselines while removing the need for fixed global ETF, demonstrating superior flexibility, simplicity, and efficiency.

papers.title: Return of Frustratingly Easy Unsupervised Video Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: The method achieves substantial absolute adaptation performance enhancement on cross-domain action recognition tasks with significantly superior relative gains over state-of-the-art baselines.

papers.title: Revisiting the Role of Pretrained Weights in Model Merging: On Near-Optimality within the Core Subspace
papers.contribution: Shows task-specific adaptations should inject primarily into the orthogonal complement of core subspace, yielding consistent improvements over state-of-the-art training-free merging methods.

papers.title: SABER: Continual Learning with Representation Conflict Management
papers.contribution: Achieves performance on par with or surpassing state-of-the-art by directly managing representational conflict.

papers.title: SaTeen: Learning Structural Alignment for Continual Test-Time Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieves SOTA performance across various TTA and continual TTA scenarios.

papers.title: Scaling Unsupervised Multi-Source Federated Domain Adaptation through Group-Wise Discrepancy Minimization
papers.contribution: State-of-the-art on standard benchmarks; significantly outperforms prior methods in large-scale settings on new Digit-18 benchmark with 18 datasets.

papers.title: Shapley Neuron Values for Continual Learning: Which Neurons Matter Most?
papers.contribution: Experiments on ImageNet-1k show that SNV consistently outperforms existing buffer-free methods

papers.title: Spectral Imbalance Causes Forgetting in Low-Rank Continual Adaptation
papers.contribution: Mitigates both backward and forward forgetting in continual learning, outperforming baselines while maintaining parameter efficiency.

papers.title: SyMerge: From Non-Interference to Synergistic Merging via Single-Layer Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results across vision, dense prediction, and NLP benchmarks, successfully merges models from different initializations.

papers.title: U$^3$CF: Unbiased, Unconfounding, and Unified Causal Framework for Multi-Target Domain Adaptation
papers.contribution: Achieve unbiased prediction by blocking confounding effects while preserving invariant semantics, with consistent outperformance on four benchmarks.

papers.title: Unlearning during Training: Domain-Specific Gradient Ascent for Domain Generalization
papers.contribution: IU consistently improves out-of-distribution generalization across seven benchmarks and fifteen baselines, achieving average accuracy gains up to 3.0%.

papers.title: What Language is This? Ask Your Tokenizer.
papers.contribution: UniLID achieves competitive performance on standard benchmarks, substantially improves sample efficiency in low-resource settings (surpassing 70% accuracy with five labeled samples per language), and delivers large gains on dialect identification.

papers.title: When Shared Knowledge Hurts: Spectral Over-Accumulation in Model Merging
papers.contribution: SVC improves strong merging baselines across vision and language benchmarks, achieving state-of-the-art performance with 13.0% improvement over Task Arithmetic.
